column1: 22238§marble§ˈmɑːbl§In this game, you can insert a marble into a small hole to open the door.§在这个游戏中，你可以往一个小洞里塞入一颗**弹珠**来把门打开。§
22239§booth§buːð§In our company, we work in separate booths.§在公司里，我们在**隔间**里工作。§
22240§imitation§ˌɪmɪˈteɪʃn§A child learns to talk by imitation.§小孩子通过**模仿**学会说话。§
22241§exceed§ɪkˈsiːd§World population in the twenty-first century will probably exceed 8 billion.§世界人口总数在21世纪有可能**超过**80亿。§

22242§cohesion§kəʊˈhiːʒn§The Women's Social and Political Union (WSPU) brought the suffragette movement the cohesion and focus it had previously lacked.§妇女社会政治同盟为妇女参政运动带来了前所未有的**凝聚力**。§改例句：英文句中的中文括号改为英文括号
22243§livestock§ˈlaɪvstɒk§The country banned the import of all ruminant livestock from Europe.§该国禁止从欧洲进口任何反刍类**家畜**。§
22244§astound§əˈstaʊnd§The eruption in May 1980 of Mount St. Helens, Washington State, astounded the world with its violence.§1980年5月，位于华盛顿的圣海伦斯火山喷发所产生的强大破坏力**震惊**了世界。§
22245§absorb§əbˈsɔːb§Trees can absorb carbon dioxide.§树木可以**吸收**二氧化碳。§
22246§decrease§dɪˈkriːs§Do you think the cinema has increased or decreased in popularity in recent years?§你认为近年来电影受欢迎的程度是提高了还是**降低**了？§
22247§moral§ˈmɒrəl§Altering our genetic inheritance is a moral problem.§改变我们的遗传基因是一个**伦理**问题。§
22248§weigh§weɪ§These boxes are heavy with honey and may weigh up to 90 pounds each.§这些装满蜂蜜的盒子非常重，每个都可能**重达**90磅。§
22249§ceramic§səˈræmɪk§Glass ceramics can serve as nose cones of missiles.§玻璃**瓷**可用来制造导弹的头锥体。§
22250§acquisition§ˌækwɪˈzɪʃn§Tom's newest acquisition is a luxurious sports car.§汤姆新**获得**了一辆豪华跑车。§
22251§character§ˈkærəktə(r)§The interview does give you a bit of information about an applicant's character.§面试确实能给你提供一些和应聘者**性格**有关的信息。§
22252§arrange§əˈreɪndʒ§The Language Institute activities coordinator can assist students to arrange any sport and leisure activities.§语言学院的活动负责人可以帮助学生**安排**任何体育和休闲活动。§
22253§conservation§ˌkɒnsəˈveɪʃn§We just set up a new wildlife conservation programme here.§我们刚刚在这里启动了一个新的野生动物**保护**项目。§
22254§earthworm§ˈɜːθwɜːm§The digested dung in these burrows is an excellent food supply for the earthworms.§这些洞里（蜣螂）消化过的粪球给**蚯蚓**提供了极好的食物来源。§

22255§entice§ɪnˈtaɪs§With the festivals coming, supermarkets begin to push out all sorts of tricks to entice customers to consume.§随着节日的来临，超市使出各种各样的手段**吸引**顾客消费。§改例句：entice sb. to 后接动词原形，consumption 改为 consume

22256§manipulative§məˈnɪpjələtɪv§To handle negative experiences, a child learns manipulative techniques that are hard to refrain from later in life or even become set patterns.§为了应对这些负面体验，儿童学会了控制自己和他人，这种**操纵**技巧在日后的生活中很难被戒除，甚至会变成既定的行为模式。§改例句：handle 是及物动词，删去 with；refrain 是不及物动词，补 from

22257§memorise§ˈmeməraɪz§Before sailing to the sea, prudent navigators will study the sailing directions, and memorise lighthouse locations to prepare themselves for any conditions they might encounter.§出海前，细心的航海员会研究航海说明并**记住**灯塔的位置，为他们可能会遇到的任何情况做准备。§

22258§retrenchment§rɪˈtrentʃmənt§Macro-control and retrenchment curbed sizable speculation venture capital in real estate, leading to the reduction of housing market demand.§宏观调控和费用**削减**抑制了大量房地产风险投资，致使住房市场需求有所减少。§

22259§motivational§ˌməʊtɪˈveɪʃənl§The science-and-engineering students have motivational, cognitive and emotional barriers in English learning, according to a survey released by the Ministry of Education.§据教育部公布的一项调查结果显示，理工科学生在英语学习中存在着**动机**、认知和情感方面的障碍。§
22260§reinforcement§ˌriːɪnˈfɔːsmənt§The Red Cross blasted the authorities' response to the disaster, making an urgent plea for reinforcements and aid.§红十字会严厉抨击当局对灾难的反应，并紧急呼吁要求**增援**和救助。§

22261§intervention§ˌɪntəˈvenʃn§In a decade, more and more governments strengthened health intervention, and introduced a series of new health-care systems.§十年间，越来越多的政府加强对保健的**干预**，引入了一些新的医疗体系。§改例句：decade 前缺冠词，补 a；a series of 后应接复数，system 改为 systems
22262§infirmity§ɪnˈfɜːməti§Pathogen infections are among the leading causes of infirmity and mortality among humans and animals in the world.§病原体感染是世界上导致人和动物**衰弱**和死亡的主要原因之一。§

22263§glossy§ˈglɒsi§All of a sudden, the sun broke through from the heavy clouds, shining on her glossy hair, giving it a metallic luster.§突然间，太阳冲破阴云，照在她**光滑**的头发上，给头发镀上了一层金属的光泽。§改例句：Out of sudden 不是英语说法，应为 All of a sudden

22264§escalate§ˈeskəleɪt§Instigated by a small number of people with ulterior motives, the demonstration quickly escalated into a riot.§在少数别有用心的人的煽动教唆下，游行示威很快**升级**演变成了一场暴动。§改例句：demon-stration 是排版断行残留，应为 demonstration
22265§extravagance§ɪkˈstrævəgəns§He lived in extravagance far beyond his means, which brought his career to a premature end and led to bankruptcy.§他过着超出他收入能力的**奢侈**生活，从而过早结束了自己的职业生涯，走向破产。§

22266§victimise§ˈvɪktɪmaɪz§The World Health Organization reported that environmentally related diseases victimise most of the African continent, followed by parts of Southeast Asia.§世界卫生组织称，与环境相关的疾病**危害**着非洲大陆的绝大部分地区，其次是东南亚的部分地区。§改例句：the most of Africa continent 语法错，应为 most of the African continent
22267§evaluation§ɪˌvæljuˈeɪʃn§Employees should make a copy of their completed Self Evaluation Form for their supervisor in advance of the review meeting.§开评审会之前，雇员应该复印一份填好的自我**评估**表交给主管。§
22268§maternal§məˈtɜːnl§Susan's maternal grandmother is still alive.§苏珊的**外**祖母还健在。§
22269§crusade§kruːˈseɪd§He made it his crusade to teach children to love books.§他把教育孩子热爱书籍作为自己的**奋斗目标**。§

22270§recalcitrant§rɪˈkælsɪtrənt§When someone is recalcitrant, he might resist following orders, or going along, even be too stubborn to deal with.§如果一个人很**桀骜不驯**，他可能拒绝服从命令或者与他人合作，甚至固执到无法应付的地步。§改例句：too stubborn 前缺谓语动词，补 be
22271§mortality§mɔːˈtæləti§Although infant mortality varies by ethnicity, deaths among infants with birth defects are similar in all groups.§尽管婴儿的**死亡率**因种族而不同，但是因出生缺陷而导致的儿童死亡在各个群体中却是类似的。§
22272§taunt§tɔːnt§People used to tease and taunt him with his cowardice.§过去人们常**嘲讽**他的胆小怕事。§
22273§disseminate§dɪˈsemɪneɪt§University libraries should aim at disseminating popular culture as well as leading the dissemination of the mainstream culture.§大学图书馆应**传播**大众文化，还要引导主流文化的传播。§

22274§sanction§ˈsæŋkʃn§The economic sanctions have long been imposed on the nation due to refusing to sign a multilateral agreement.§由于拒绝签署多边协议，长久以来，这个国家一直遭受着经济**制裁**。§改例句：可数名词单数 multilateral agreement 前缺冠词，补 a
22275§invert§ɪnˈvɜːt§Should the image formed on the retina be inverted?§在视网膜上形成的图像应该是**颠倒**的吗？§改例句：去掉问号前的空格
22276§unfortunately§ʌnˈfɔːtʃənətli§Unfortunately, they cannot come to our party.§很**遗憾**，他们不能来参加我们的聚会了。§
22277§frustration§frʌˈstreɪʃn§However, you have to admit that you need him so much when the moment of sadness, fear or an acute sense of frustration descends.§但你不得不承认的是，当悲伤、痛苦或是极度**沮丧**的时候，你如此需要他。§
22278§recipe§ˈresəpi§Errors in the genetic recipe for haemoglobin give rise to the most common single-gene disorder in the world.§血红蛋白中遗传**密码**出现问题会导致世界上最常见的单基因病变。§
22279§condense§kənˈdens§This article has been adapted and condensed from the article by William and Slater.§这篇文章改编自威廉姆和斯莱特的文章，并进行了**精简**。§

22280§gather§ˈgæðə(r)§At the beginning of a new semester, all the new students will gather in the playground to meet the principal and the rest of the faculty.§新学期伊始，所有的新生在操场上**集合**与校长和其他老师见面。§改例句：「在…开始时」应为 At the beginning of，In 错
22281§advertise§ˈædvətaɪz§The total number of jobs advertised in the journal was 120.§这本杂志上**刊登**了120个职位。§
22282§utility§juːˈtɪləti§One of many reforms came in the area of public utilities.§众多改革措施中有一条涉及**公用事业**的变革。§
22283§exhibit§ɪgˈzɪbɪt§Some of the exhibits at the museum are very precious.§这个博物馆的一些**展品**非常珍贵。§
22284§irrevocable§ɪˈrevəkəbl§The powers given to these agents are irrevocable.§下放给这些代理商的权力是**不可改变**的。§
22285§shelter§ˈʃeltə(r)§Harbour is a physical concept, a shelter for ships, while port is an economic concept, a centre of land-sea exchange.§Harbour是物质概念，即船的“**家**”；而port是经济概念，即海陆货物交换的中心。§
22286§stock§stɒk§Fish stocks here began to decline in the 1950s in South Scotland.§在苏格兰南部，鱼类**储量**从20世纪50年代开始减少。§
22287§devise§dɪˈvaɪz§Ford devised the first moving auto assembly line.§福特**发明**了第一条移动的汽车装配线。§
22288§career§kəˈrɪə(r)§The idea of having a single career is becoming old fashioned.§只从事一种**职业**的想法现在已经开始变得落伍了。§
22289§humidity§hjuːˈmɪdəti§The wooden frame warped in the humidity.§木框因受**潮**而弯曲了。§
22290§hollow§ˈhɒləʊ§Dung beetles' homes are hollowed out from within.§蜣螂的家是从里面往外**挖空**的。§
22291§statistic§stəˈtɪstɪk§The writer pointed out that the employment statistic was deceptive.§作者指出这个就业**统计数据**不可信。§
22292§bark§bɑːk§Our neighbour's dog barks constantly.§邻居家的狗总是**叫**个不停。§
22293§burrow§ˈbʌrəʊ§Most dung beetles burrow into the soil and bury dung in tunnels.§大多数蜣螂在地下**挖洞**，并将粪球埋在地下。§
22294§equivalent§ɪˈkwɪvələnt§At that time, the cost of a bulb was equivalent to half a day's pay for the average worker.§那时，一个灯泡的成本**相当于**普通工人半天的工资。§
22295§fatigue§fəˈtiːg§Part-time workers are less likely to succumb to fatigue in stressful jobs.§兼职工人在有压力的工作中不太可能被**疲劳**压垮。§
22296§bibliography§ˌbɪbliˈɒgrəfi§I'm looking for those books which my professor lists in the bibliography.§我正在找教授列在**参考书目**单上的那些书。§

22297§probable§ˈprɒbəbl§It is probable that, some time in the tenth century, gun powder was first compounded from its basic ingredients of saltpetre, charcoal and sulphur.§火药**很可能**最早在十世纪的某个时间由硝石、木炭和硫磺等基本成分混合而成。§
22298§treadmill§ˈtredmɪl§I can't get off the office treadmill.§我无法摆脱**单调**的坐班工作。§
22299§flavour§ˈfleɪvə(r)§Each country's coffee has a different flavour.§各国的咖啡都别具**风味**。§
22300§asymmetry§ˌeɪˈsɪmətri§Asymmetry is a common feature of the human body.§**不对称**是人体共同的特点。§
22301§lethal§ˈliːθl§Bugs and weeds become resistant to poisons, so next year's poisons must be more lethal.§臭虫和野草对农药产生了抗药性，所以来年农药的**杀伤力**就需要再强一些。§
22302§stare§steə(r)§He stared at the word trying to remember what it meant.§他**盯着**这个单词，努力想记住它的意思。§
22303§colony§ˈkɒləni§Different animals in the colony had different manifestations of the disease.§同一**群体**的不同动物对同一疾病有不同的表现形式。§
22304§stab§stæb§Such a vicious lie could be nothing but a stab in the back.§这样一种恶毒的谎言简直是在背后**捅**刀子。§改译文：「暗箭伤人」是成语，括不出 stab（刺，捅），改为「在背后捅刀子」
22305§fingerprint§ˈfɪŋgəprɪnt§Systems using fingerprints, hands, voices and faces are already on the market.§市场上已出现了利用**指纹**、手印、声音和面部进行识别的系统。§
22306§enthusiasm§ɪnˈθjuːziæzəm§She shows great enthusiasm for the movie.§她对这部电影表现出极大的**热情**。§
